THE ACTUAL RESIDUAL IS 6, ON A NEWER BASELINE. Run 266 (sqc-0.5.0-a23385b3): 87 findings, 81 labeled, 6 unlabeled. Run 267 (sqc-0.5.0-c4c3ec58): 84 findings, 78 labeled, 6 unlabeled. The 266->267 drop from 81 to 78 labeled is existing labels whose keys stopped firing, not new unlabeled work. This batch labels those 6.

ALLOCATION-SIZE HOLD (aurora_lint 1298): ZERO held. None of the 6 is an allocation-size finding -- all are compound-addition accumulators (rio buffer/conn positions, a byte counter, a replication stat), so the hardcoded-32-bit wraps_32_size_t gate does not apply to any of them. Nothing was withheld from this batch for any reason.

VERDICTS: 6/6 FP (5 high confidence, 1 medium). Consistent with the existing valkey INT30-C baseline of 77 FP / 4 TP. Two are strictly dominated by a guard on or near the flagged line (rio.c:73, rio.c:265) and one by the read_limit check at rio.c:236 (rio.c:264); the rest are bounded-domain (a size_t or long long byte counter cannot reach 2^64 in one process lifetime).

NOT A MISFIRE, CHECKED DELIBERATELY. Four of the six increment a SIGNED lvalue (off_t pos, long long stat_net_repl_input_bytes) while the message says 'unsigned integer compound addition', which looks like an ADR-0005 misfire. It is not: in `E1 += E2` the usual arithmetic conversions apply to E1 + E2, and with E2 a size_t the signed lvalue converts to unsigned, so the addition really is unsigned. No misfire task filed; aurora-lint's wording is correct here.

FP-REFUTATION PASS: run over all 6 rather than the medium row alone, since the batch came back 100% FP and FP-refutation is the useful adversarial direction. Each FP was challenged on whether `len` could be attacker-controlled to a wrapping magnitude and whether the dominating guard really dominates. All 6 survived. The one row moved off 'high' as a result is rdb.c:3096, where the challenge that landed is not the wrap but the store-back: the unsigned sum is assigned to a signed long long, so a value above LLONG_MAX is implementation-defined. That is an INT31-C/INT32-C conversion question at the same unreachable magnitude, recorded in the row's reason for a reviewer to take further if they disagree.
